text: What stops an AI from just changing the test, so it passes?
In our pipeline, tests are written first. And they must fail.
If they pass before any code exists, the run stops.
Here's a real run. Sixteen new tests, failing, because the feature doesn't exist yet.
Then they're committed. That commit hash is the lock.
After every coding attempt, the script diffs the test folder against that lock.
One changed line? Guard failed. The run stops.
Don't ask the AI to be honest. Make cheating detectable.
